agent: L.7.2 Adversarial RED — SSRF + External Fetch
mission: Hunt every Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vector. Any place the backend opens a network socket / fetches a URL where the destination is influenced by user input (admin or otherwise) is in scope. Verify: webhook callback URLs, image URL fetching, external service calls (Stripe/Senangpay/FCM/SMS/mail), OAuth/SSO callback, OEmbed/preview, loyalty QR generation, PDF generation, CSV/Excel import. Confirm: allowlist + IP block + DNS-rebind protection on every user-controlled destination.
scope: Code-static read-only audit of every outbound HTTP/socket callsite in app/. Zero file modifications outside this findings JSON. No live exploit run (Le Cayenne single-box LAN deploy, no public ingress, no AWS metadata to exfil — SSRF lateral impact is laptop-local). Documenting the V1.0.2 cloud-prep gap so the host allowlist is in place BEFORE owner initiates AWS cutover (per feedback_no_cloud_until_owner_initiates.md mandate).
method: grep-survey of every Http::/GuzzleHttp/curl_exec/fopen/fsockopen/file_get_contents/addMediaFromUrl/stream_socket callsite. For each: trace the destination — hardcoded constant, hardcoded SDK endpoint, env config, DB-stored config (admin-settable), or request-body field. Flag every request-body or DB-admin path as SSRF candidate. Cross-check authorization layer (route middleware, FormRequest authorize, permission gate). Map blast radius (read response? write only? socket open only?). Compare with sibling protections (CSRF except list, throttle middleware, boot guards).

ssrf_vectors_audited.destinations: admin POST /api/admin/mail with body { mail_host: '169.254.169.254', mail_port: 80, ... } → MailService::update writes MAIL_HOST=169.254.169.254 to .env via EnvEditor → optimize:clear → subsequent Mail::send connects to that host (Symfony Mailer SMTP transport).
constraints: permission:settings required (admin/owner role only — MailController:18 middleware)
Single-tenant V1 Le Cayenne — only the owner has permission:settings
Writes .env which is loaded for the WHOLE Laravel app, then config:clear forces re-read
Validation in MailRequest:25-36 = string|max:190 — NO IP block, NO host allowlist
No DNS-rebind protection (host string is resolved by libc gethostbyname)
Outbound SMTP starttls handshake will fail on most non-SMTP services (port 25/465/587 expected), but bind-only signal still leaks port-open state via timing
ssrf_vectors_audited.blast_radius: Cloud (AWS): SMTP → 169.254.169.254:80 — handshake fails but TCP connect timing leaks metadata-service presence. LAN: SMTP → 192.168.x.x:25 leaks internal mail-server map. Limited because outbound is one-shot per mail-send-attempt (no read-back of response body via mail flow). Admin needs to trigger mail send (e.g. password reset, order confirmation) to fire the SMTP connect.
ssrf_vectors_audited.verdict: EXPLOITABLE-BY-ADMIN — single-tenant V1 LAN risk is laptop-local (owner already controls the box), but FUTURE V2 SaaS with multi-tenant admin = critical. Document as V1.0.X cloud-prep backlog item BEFORE owner initiates cloud cutover.

ssrf_vectors_audited.vector: ESC/POS printer host (TcpPrinterTransport fsockopen to admin-settable Printer.host)
ssrf_vectors_audited.destinations: admin POST /api/admin/printer with body { type: 'escpos_tcp', host: '169.254.169.254', port: 80, ... } → store as Printer row → admin GET /api/admin/printer/{id}/test-print → EscPosPrinterService::testPrint → TcpPrinterTransport::send → @fsockopen((string) $host, $port, ..., 2.0) writes 50-200 bytes of ESC/POS data + closes.
constraints: permission:pos required for testPrint (PrinterController:19) — POS Operator role has this
Branch-isolated: PrinterRequest:45-54 forces branch_id = user's branch_id for non-admin users (single-tenant Le Cayenne = only branch 0 admin can do this anyway)
Validation in PrinterRequest:31-37 = host string|max:64 + port integer|min:1|max:65535 — NO IP block, NO allowlist, NO DNS-rebind protection
Write-only socket: TcpPrinterTransport sends bytes + closes (no response read back to attacker)

Timing/error leakage: tcp_open_failed:errstr(errno) returned in transport->lastError() → response 502 ok:false on testPrint → admin can probe port-open vs port-closed vs filtered via TCP connect timing
ssrf_vectors_audited.blast_radius: Cloud (AWS post-cutover): admin can port-scan internal VPC subnets via repeated testPrint with different host/port. Cannot READ response data (ESC/POS is write-only), but can MAP internal services. AWS metadata exfil = blocked (metadata service IMDSv2 requires GET + token header, not socket write). LAN single-box: laptop-local, owner controls the box anyway.
ssrf_vectors_audited.verdict: EXPLOITABLE-BY-ADMIN (V1 LAN: laptop-local) — port-scan primitive for any admin/pos-permission holder. CRITICAL for V2 multi-tenant SaaS where Branch Managers gain printer config. Document as V1.0.X cloud-prep backlog item.

ssrf_vectors_audited.vector: LanguageService LFI/RFI via file_get_contents + include + file_put_contents on user-supplied path
ssrf_vectors_audited.destinations:
POST /api/admin/language/file-text with { path: '...', name: '...' } → LanguageController::fileText (permission:settings, LanguageController:27) → LanguageService::fileText line 187+189 `include($request->path)` — NO path validation, NO base_path() containment.

POST /api/admin/language/file-text-store with { x_language_file_path: '...', ... } → LanguageService::fileTextStore line 201 `fopen($request->x_language_file_path, 'rw')` line 202 `file_get_contents($request->x_language_file_path)` line 214 `file_put_contents($request->x_language_file_path, $fileContent)` — NO path validation, NO containment.
constraints: file_get_contents() ACCEPTS PHP stream wrappers including http://, https://, ftp://, php://, data://, phar://, expect:// (depending on PHP build) — this is a TRUE SSRF + LFI + RFI gadget
include() on the same path = RCE (remote PHP include if allow_url_include=On — usually Off in modern PHP, but php://input is always available)
file_put_contents on attacker-controlled path = arbitrary file write (LFW)

Existing P0 SEC-RCE comment at LanguageController:23-27 says '[P0 SEC-RCE] fileText (include() = LFI) + fileTextStore (file_put_contents = arbitrary…)' — known weakness already flagged, only permission:settings is the mitigation
ssrf_vectors_audited.blast_radius: Full RCE (via include with php://input or known writable file), arbitrary file read (file_get_contents with php://filter base64-encode for binary), arbitrary file write (file_put_contents to any path Laravel user can write), and SSRF (http:// wrapper in file_get_contents — read response body returned to admin via 422 message or include() output).
ssrf_vectors_audited.verdict: KNOWN P0 SEC-RCE — mitigated solely by permission:settings + single-tenant trust boundary. The in-code comment proves the team knew the issue and accepted the risk for V1 single-tenant. CRITICAL gap for V2 SaaS — must be hardened with allowlist + base_path() containment + reject stream-wrapper schemes BEFORE owner initiates cloud cutover.

findings.title: Printer host SSRF — admin can fsockopen to arbitrary internal/metadata IP via PrinterController

evidence.source_of_host: Printer.host column, set by admin via POST/PUT /api/admin/printer (app/Http/Controllers/Admin/PrinterController.php:37-68 — permission:settings middleware)
evidence.trigger: admin GET /api/admin/printer/{id}/test-print (permission:pos middleware — POS Operator can also fire this) → EscPosPrinterService::testPrint at app/Services/Hardware/EscPosPrinterService.php:50-79 → calls sendRaw → calls TcpPrinterTransport::send → fsockopen with admin-set host:port
evidence.validation_gap: app/Http/Requests/Admin/PrinterRequest.php:31-37 — host = ['nullable', 'string', 'max:64'], port = ['nullable', 'integer', 'min:1', 'max:65535']. NO IP-range block (no rfc1918, no link-local 169.254.0.0/16, no loopback 127.0.0.0/8, no IPv6 ::1 / fe80::/10), NO DNS-rebind defense (TOCTOU between validation hostname-resolve and fsockopen hostname-resolve), NO allowlist.

exploit_walkthrough: 1. Admin (or any permission:settings holder) POSTs /api/admin/printer with body: { name: 'mdtest', branch_id: 1, type: 'escpos_tcp', host: '169.254.169.254', port: 80, station: 'receipt', width_chars: 48, status: 1 }.
2. Validation PASSES (string|max:64, integer|1-65535 — no IP blocklist).
3. Printer row id=42 created with host='169.254.169.254' port=80.
4. Admin (or permission:pos holder = POS Operator role) GETs /api/admin/printer/42/test-print.
5. TcpPrinterTransport::send opens TCP to 169.254.169.254:80 with 2.0s timeout, writes ~80 bytes of ESC/POS bytes (init + codepage + text + cut), closes.
6. Response body: { ok: false, printer_id: 42 } with HTTP 502 IF connection failed (cloud metadata service doesn't speak ESC/POS, will close).
7. Response body: { ok: true, printer_id: 42 } with HTTP 200 IF TCP socket opened AND wrote all bytes successfully (timing/port-open signal).
8. Attacker can iterate host/port combos to map internal VPC (AWS post-cutover) or LAN subnet.
findings.blast_radius: V1 Le Cayenne LAN single-box: laptop-local (owner already controls the box, no external attacker — RISK = NEGLIGIBLE). V2 SaaS cloud post-cutover: Branch Manager / POS Operator role gains internal-VPC port-scan primitive — CRITICAL escalation.
findings.fix: Add a host-validation rule in PrinterRequest that: (a) refuses non-FQDN strings containing IP-literal chars unless they match an explicit allowlist of CIDR ranges (e.g. 192.168.0.0/16 only — typical LAN printer range), (b) refuses 169.254.0.0/16 + 127.0.0.0/8 + ::1 + fe80::/10 + 0.0.0.0/8 outright, (c) optionally DNS-resolve FQDN and re-validate the resolved IP against the same blocklist (loose DNS-rebind defense — full defense requires post-resolve binding via curl-style CURLOPT_RESOLVE which fsockopen does not support — defer to V1.0.2). Sentinel: tests/Feature/Sentinels/PrinterHostAllowlistSentinelTest validating PrinterRequest rejects 169.254.169.254 / 127.0.0.1 / ::1 inputs.

findings.title: SMTP host SSRF — admin can point MAIL_HOST to arbitrary internal IP via MailController

evidence.source_of_host: Request body field 'mail_host', set by admin via PUT/PATCH /api/admin/mail (app/Http/Controllers/Admin/MailController.php:30-37 — permission:settings middleware)
evidence.trigger: Any subsequent Mail::send call from Laravel (password reset, order confirmation, invoice email, etc.) — Symfony Mailer SMTP transport opens TCP to MAIL_HOST:MAIL_PORT with starttls handshake.
evidence.validation_gap: app/Http/Requests/MailRequest.php:28-29 — mail_host = ['required', 'string', 'max:190'], mail_port = ['required', 'string', 'max:190']. NO IP-range block, NO allowlist, NO DNS-rebind defense.

exploit_walkthrough: 1. Admin PUTs /api/admin/mail with body: { mail_host: '169.254.169.254', mail_port: '80', mail_username: 'x', mail_password: 'x', mail_encryption: 'none', mail_from_name: 'x', mail_from_email: 'x@x' }.
3. MailService::update writes MAIL_HOST=169.254.169.254 + MAIL_PORT=80 to .env via Dipokhalder\EnvEditor + Artisan::call('optimize:clear').

4. Subsequent Mail::send → Symfony Mailer connects to 169.254.169.254:80 — handshake fails (no SMTP greeting), but TCP connect timing + error message ('Connection could not be established with host 169.254.169.254:80 stream_socket_client(): Unable to connect…') is logged to storage/logs/laravel.log.
5. Attacker (admin) iterates host/port via mail-send triggers, maps internal VPC.
findings.blast_radius: V1 LAN: laptop-local. V2 SaaS: tenant-admin gains internal-VPC probe primitive. Additional risk: if MAIL_HOST is set to a credential-collection honeypot ('attacker.com:25'), every mail-send leaks SMTP-AUTH credentials in cleartext (LOGIN auth) — this is admin-on-self though (admin set their own MAIL_HOST), so impact is limited to their own outbound mail metadata.
findings.fix: Add IP blocklist + allowlist of TLD/MX-style values in MailRequest:28-29. Reject 169.254.0.0/16, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1, fe80::/10. Optionally enforce TLD presence (must contain '.', cannot be bare IP unless on explicit allowlist). Sentinel: tests/Feature/Sentinels/MailHostAllowlistSentinelTest.

findings.title: LanguageService LFI/RFI/SSRF gadget — pre-existing P0 SEC-RCE flagged in code, gated only by permission:settings

evidence.source_of_path: request body fields 'path' and 'x_language_file_path' — admin-supplied, validated only as 'required, string' in LanguageFileTextGetRequest:25-31 (no path normalization, no base_path() containment)
evidence.validation_gap: ZERO path validation beyond 'string'. file_get_contents/fopen accept PHP stream wrappers (http://, https://, php://, php://input, php://filter, data://, phar://, ftp://, ssh2:// if ext loaded). include() of remote PHP IF allow_url_include=On (default Off in PHP 7+).
evidence.team_awareness: Comment at LanguageController:23-27 explicitly labels this as '[P0 SEC-RCE]' — known issue accepted for V1 single-tenant trust boundary.

exploit_walkthrough_ssrf: 2. file_exists('http://169.254.169.254/...') returns TRUE if URL is reachable (PHP stream wrapper).
3. include() loads response body AS PHP — if response is non-PHP (typical metadata service JSON), echoes content to output buffer + may trigger PHP parse warnings.
4. Response body leaks to admin via stdout / 422 error message.

5. Alternative: POST /api/admin/language/file-text-store with x_language_file_path = 'php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...' → file_get_contents reads the URL, str_replace operates on the content, file_put_contents tries to write back (fails — stream is read-only) but the read leak already happened (response body returned to admin).
findings.blast_radius: Full SSRF (read internal HTTP services via file_get_contents wrapper) + arbitrary local file read (file://, php://filter base64) + arbitrary local file write (file_put_contents to ANY writable path) + potential RCE (file_put_contents PHP code to a public/ accessible .php path → browse to it). V1 single-tenant: owner-on-self risk only. V2 SaaS: TENANT ADMIN COMPROMISE = HOST COMPROMISE.
findings.fix: Before V2 SaaS cutover: refactor LanguageService::fileText + fileTextStore to (a) accept only language code + filename (not raw path), (b) compute path internally as resource_path('lang/' . $code . '/' . basename($name)), (c) realpath() the result and assert str_starts_with($realpath, realpath(resource_path('lang')) . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR), (d) refuse $name containing '..', '/', '\\', or null byte, (e) refuse $code not matching /^[a-z]{2,5}(-[A-Z]{2})?$/. Sentinel: tests/Feature/Sentinels/LanguageServicePathContainmentSentinelTest with negative tests for http://, php://, data://, file://, ../etc/passwd, /etc/passwd, php://input.
findings.note: V1 ACCEPTED RISK per existing in-code comment — owner trust boundary. CANNOT proceed to V2 SaaS without hardening this.

verdict.v1_le_cayenne_lan_release_status: GREEN — single-box LAN deploy, owner controls everything, no public ingress, no AWS metadata to exfil. All 3 user-controlled SSRF/LFI vectors are gated by permission:settings (owner-only), and the trust boundary is the laptop itself. ZERO release blockers for V1.
verdict.v2_saas_cloud_cutover_status: RED-BLOCKED — 3 P0/P1 findings (L7-2-F-01 printer host, L7-2-F-02 mail host, L7-2-F-03 LanguageService LFI/RFI/SSRF gadget) MUST be hardened with host allowlist + path containment BEFORE owner initiates AWS cutover. Tenant-admin compromise pattern = host compromise pattern.
verdict.fix_complexity: Low (1-2 days of work) — add IP/host validation rules in 2 FormRequests + refactor 1 service to use resource_path containment + 3 sentinel tests. No frozen-zone touch required. No NF525 impact.

top_3_ssrf_vectors: 1. LanguageService LFI/RFI/SSRF gadget (L7-2-F-03) — KNOWN P0 SEC-RCE in code comment, gated only by permission:settings. Full RCE + SSRF + LFW gadget. V2 SaaS cutover blocker.
2. Printer host fsockopen (L7-2-F-01) — admin sets Printer.host to arbitrary IP, testPrint fires TCP connect. Internal-VPC port-scan primitive. V2 SaaS cutover blocker.
3. SMTP host (L7-2-F-02) — admin sets MAIL_HOST in .env to arbitrary IP, mail-send triggers TCP connect. Internal-VPC probe primitive. V2 SaaS cutover blocker.
recommendations: P0 — Before V2 SaaS cutover: refactor LanguageService::fileText + fileTextStore to use code+filename interface with resource_path() containment; add LanguageServicePathContainmentSentinelTest negative-input suite.

P1 — Before V2 SaaS cutover: add IP blocklist (rfc1918 + link-local + loopback) and optional allowlist to PrinterRequest and MailRequest; add PrinterHostAllowlistSentinelTest + MailHostAllowlistSentinelTest.

P2 — Defense-in-depth: enforce a Laravel HTTP-client middleware that strips Stream wrappers (http://, php://, data://, etc) from any URL-typed user input across all FormRequests; central rules helper App\Rules\SafeRemoteHost.

P3 — Production boot guard: refuse to BOOT if MAIL_HOST or any Printer.host in DB matches a blocklist IP — promotes runtime detection to startup-fail-closed (mirrors AppServiceProvider:78-145 NF525 boot guards pattern).
P3 — Observability: log every TCP connect attempt from TcpPrinterTransport with host+port+resolved_ip+source_user_id to a dedicated 'hardware' log channel — port-scan attempts become alertable.
